correctness.rationale: For a fixed deck element of positive reduced length, the tree-lift normal form reduces all off-axis backtracks and swaps neighboring opposite axis steps. Each lift component has a constant vertex-0 bipartition parity; its centralizer identifies the two parities iff the primitive axis period is odd. At geodesic length all maps are rigid because the Petersen graph has no squares. Matsushita (arXiv:2412.19144, Theorem 1.4) supplies contractible lift components and the published square-free-target trichotomy supplies the null component. Counting primitive rooted cyclic periods by the explicit Hashimoto matrix and Möbius inversion then yields the formula. A genuinely independent enumeration of every cyclic recoloring component for 3<=n<=12 agrees; this bounded check is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A single exact computation of all infinitely many source-length Hom homotopy types for a canonical cubic high-girth target is a natural classification problem. The primitive period parity centralizer distinction is essential: at source length twelve, twice-wound pentagons yield 24 rather than 48 circle components. The formula converts a graph-Hom component census into the explicit Ihara nonbacktracking trace sequence and determines all Betti ranks and component counts for every n, beyond isolated previously calculated examples.
